faqs.q: What is the Australia lowest salary for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The Australia lowest salary is the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How does the National Minimum Wage compare to award rates?

For example, the minimum award wage in some awards may be above $26.44 per hour. Always check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool to find the correct minimum wage for your job.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the Australia lowest salary?

So if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, your employer must also contribute an additional 12% superannuation on top of your gross pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Australia Lowest Salary

When people ask about the **australia lowest salary**, they are usually referring to the legal minimum an employer can pay an employee. In Australia, this floor is set by the National Minimum Wage, reviewed annually by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1004.90 per week** based on a 38-hour week, as confirmed by the. This rate applies to employees who are not covered by an award or registered agreement.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is straightforward. For example, at the National Minimum Wage:

- $26.44 × 38 hours × 52 weeks = **$52,241.44 per year** (gross, before tax and super).

If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The same formula applies: multiply your hourly rate by your usual weekly hours, then by 52. This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employees are paid fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. For the National Minimum Wage:

- Weekly: $1004.90
- Fortnightly: **$2009.80**

This can help when budgeting or comparing salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the **minimum legal floor**, but most employees are covered by an industry or occupation award that sets higher minimum rates. The explains that award wages are the minimum for most workers. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Award may have pay rates above $26.44 per hour, depending on the classification and experience level. Always check the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool or their [pay guides](/blog) to ensure you are being paid correctly.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum wage to compensate for not receiving paid leave entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is:

- $26.44 × 1.25 = **$33.05 per hour**

This loading is added to the base hourly rate. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to apply the 25% casual loading on top of the base rate you enter. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it separately.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Superannuation (super) is an additional payment your employer must make into a super fund on your behalf. The super guarantee rate for 2026–27 is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your gross salary. There is a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, your employer contributes an extra 12% of your ordinary earnings to super. This means your total remuneration package is higher than your gross pay.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your total taxable income and the tax rates for 2026–27. The resident tax-free threshold is $18,200, then:

- 15% for income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% for income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% for income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% for income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage ($52,241.44), the estimated tax and Medicare would be around $7,200–$7,500 per year, leaving a take-home pay of roughly $44,700–$45,000. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Key Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

The National Minimum Wage is the lowest legal rate, but average earnings are much higher. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week as of May 2026. That equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 for a 38-hour week. The gap between the minimum wage and average earnings highlights the importance of checking your award or agreement to ensure you are paid fairly.

### When the National Minimum Wage Doesn't Apply

Some employees have different minimum wages:

- **Junior employees** (under 21) receive a percentage of the National Minimum Wage based on age.
- **Apprentices and trainees** have special minimum wage rates set by the Miscellaneous Award.
- **Employees with disability** may have a percentage rate if their productivity is affected.

For these groups, the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more details.

### Summary

The **australia lowest salary** is the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week. Most workers are covered by awards with higher rates. Casual employees get 25% loading, and super is paid on top. Use the formula hourly × hours × 52 to estimate annual gross pay, and remember that tax and Medicare reduce your take-home amount. Always verify your correct minimum wage using official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman or Fair Work Commission.
